Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - post-demo & numbers

Hi Rachel - great demo earlier, thanks for your time. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can fast-track a Dedicated pricing proposal: 

- Recap of high-level needs: production LLM features for the ACME Assistant (LLM-based summarization + routing), target model family: Llama-3-70B (few-shot), want predictable latency and data isolation (dedicated).
- Key items we need from you to size dedicated capacity and produce unit economics: token volumes (daily/monthly), average tokens per request, peak concurrency/requests per second, desired latency SLOs, and a target budget or $/1M tokens target.
- Preference on GPU class: A100 vs H100 (H100 usually gives better throughput for 70B-class models but at higher instance cost).

From our side we will provide: an example config for Reserved Capacity (GPUs + shard layout), throughput estimates (tokens/sec & RPS), and a target unit cost (USD per 1M tokens) including the assumptions (batching factor, prefix cache hit rate, quantization level).

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v2.pdf (pricing + config examples).

Can you confirm the numbers below or send the traffic sample you mentioned on the call? Once we have that we can model 2-3 capacity options and pick one that hits your target $/1M tokens.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- You: share monthly token volumes + sample traffic (CSV) by EOD tomorrow if possible.
- Us: Deliver 3 reserved-capacity options (cost + throughput + expected unit $/1M tokens) within 48 hours of receiving samples.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa - useful recap. Per the call, here are the initial numbers from our TRAFFIC team: \n\
- Typical: ~200M tokens/day (roughly ~6B tokens/month)
- Peak day: up to 350M tokens/day
- Avg tokens/request: 1,500 (few-shot prompts + output)
- Peak concurrency estimate: ~10 concurrent requests sustained during spikes (~30s-60s windows)
- Target latency: P95 < 600ms for streaming text generation (lower is better but this is our SLO)
- Preference: H100 preferred if the price delta vs A100 is within ~20% given performance win.
- Budget range: $30k- $40k / month for inference (we can consider larger if the unit economics are very compelling).
- Target unit: our finance team asked for a target ~ $5- $7 per 1M tokens (rough target to evaluate).

I've attached a small sample CSV (acme_traffic_samples.csv) showing hourly token distribution for the last 30 days. Happy to hop on a pricing deep-dive next week.

- Rachel Lang
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - numbers from ACME (see below)

Quick internal note after Rachel's reply - numbers look solid. Initial sizing thoughts (ballpark) to put against ACME's targets: \n\
- Workload: Llama-3-70B (few-shot), avg 1.5k tokens per request, peak ~350M tokens/day (~4,050 tokens/sec average across 24h; peaks ~4x that for short windows).
- Recommended GPU class: H100 for best throughput on 70B with FP16 / quantization-friendly setup; A100 could be a lower-cost option but may require more GPUs to hit latency targets.

Config options (3 tiers):
1) Small (cost-conscious): 4 x A100 (reserved) - estimated sustained throughput ~20k tokens/sec with aggressive batching; estimated unit cost ~ $9- $11 per 1M tokens. May miss P95 <600ms during spikes unless we reserve burst nodes.
2) Recommended (balanced): 4 x H100 (reserved) + 1 burst H100 - estimated sustained throughput ~50k tokens/sec, peak handling with burst; estimated unit cost ~ $5.5- $7 per 1M tokens depending on cache hit rate and batching (this hits ACME's target band).
3) High-throughput: 8 x H100 (reserved) - estimated sustained throughput ~110k tokens/sec, lower latencies and headroom for growth; estimated unit cost ~ $4- $5 per 1M tokens but higher monthly committed cost.

Assumptions that materially affect unit $/1M tokens: batching factor (we model 8-16x), prefix cache hit rate (we modeled 20-40% hit), and model quantization (FP16 vs 4-bit). We'll run the traffic sample through our cost model to produce line-item estimates with sensitivity ranges.

Next internal steps: I'll run the CSV through the cost model and produce a price matrix (tokens/month vs config) + a short doc that maps to ACME's $30k- $40k/month target. If we can hit ~$6/1M tokens with 4xH100 + burst, that's the sweet spot to propose.

- Marcus
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

(Onward to modeling - assigning to Vanessa for cost sensitivity analysis.)
